_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when locating a bug in an unfamiliar codebase, tracing a failure from symptom to source, or choosing between…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "this route returns 500 but I have no idea where the failure starts — walk me through finding the boundary"
cases.context: The agent has access to the problem-locating-solving skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is problem-locating-solving the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes problem-locating-solving as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against diagnosis, pattern-recognition, lint-overlay
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the problem-locating-solving workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore problem-locating-solving
Does not route to diagnosis, pattern-recognition, lint-overlay when the problem-locating-solving scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

Routes the work to diagnosis or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
